decisions.quote: To test these predictions, we experimentally manipulated misinformation availability (high vs. low) and presented double or single misinformation. However, double versus single misinformation presentation did not affect performance or interact with misinformation availability and participants frequently reported misinformation while fully detecting discrepancies between items.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The supplied primary source file (7739d78c26609886.txt) contains only the article title ('Double misinformation and eyewitness performance: An experimental replication' by Ewa Smołka and Hartmut Blank) and abstract; the introduction, methods, results, discussion, and reference list are not present. Although the title and abstract establish an empirical replication manipulating misinformation availability (high vs. low) and double vs. single misinformation presentation, the abstract never names or cites the prior study being retested, which is why the blind target has empty citation fields. Shipped row 1547 (Blank, Panday, Edwards, Skopicz-Radkiewicz, Gibson, & Reddy, 2022, 'Double misinformation: Effects on eyewitness remembering.', DOI 10.1016/j.jarmac.2021.08.001) shares authorship and topic and is very likely the original study being replicated, but the unresolved question is that the abstract-only source text does not provide the citation needed to verify whether target_index 0 is already represented by shipped row 1547 or retests a distinct absent original. (Note: Luna's duplicate_quote failed mechanical validation because it quoted the shipped row title, which is not present in the source text.)
